title: Liposuction - Impact on Pain in lipedema patients
summary:
Lipedema is a chronic, progressive condition characterized by a disorder of fat distribution resulting in a marked disproportion between the trunk and the extremities. This condition arises from a localized, symmetrical proliferation of subcutaneous adipose tissue in the lower and/or upper extremities. Characteristic features include heightened tenderness to pressure and, typically, persistent spontaneous pain.
Lipedema is classified based on morphological changes in the arms and legs. Stage 1 presents with uniformly thickened subcutaneous tissue; Stage 2 exhibits an uneven, wave-like skin surface with nodular thickening of the subcutaneous tissue; and Stage 3 is characterized by pronounced increases in circumference and overhanging tissue.
The aim of the study is to examine the course of pain before and after surgery and to gain insight into the expected pain progression. Furthermore, the study seeks to investigate changes in skin sensitivity following liposuction and to determine how laboratory parameters are affected by the procedure.
To this end, female patients diagnosed with lipedema who are scheduled to undergo one or more liposuction procedures are being enrolled in the study.

interventions.name: Observational Study: Pain assessement before the operation, after 1 week, 6 weeks and after completion of all operations with SF-12, WHO-5, Germain Pain Questionaire und PDI. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Female patients with diagnosed stage 1–3 lipedema and planned liposuction of the lower extremities, with at least 6 months of compression therapy.
Exclusion criteria:
Age <18 years, long-term anticoagulant medication, malignancy, lack of consent, coagulation disorder
